questions.question: The Khilafat Movement was associated with which of the following communities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Muslim**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Khilafat Movement was initiated by the Muslim community in India in 1919 to protect the Ottoman Caliphate after World War I.
 
• It aimed to pressure the British government to preserve the sovereignty of the Ottoman Sultan, who was also regarded as the Caliph of Islam.
 
• Leaders such as Maulana Mohammad Ali and Maulana Shaukat Ali played pivotal roles in organizing and leading the movement.
 
• The Khilafat Movement was closely linked to the Indian freedom struggle and received support from Mahatma Gandhi as part of the Non-Cooperation Movement.
 
• The movement eventually declined by 1924 following the abolition of the Caliphate by Mustafa Kemal Atatürk in Turkey.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ottoman Caliphate:** The Ottoman Caliphate was the Islamic Caliphate under the Ottoman Empire, symbolizing religious and political unity for Muslims.
 
• **World War I Impact:** The Ottoman Empire's defeat in World War I led to its partition, threatening the Caliphate's existence and prompting the Khilafat Movement.
 
• **Non-Cooperation Movement:** Mahatma Gandhi supported the Khilafat Movement, integrating it into the broader struggle against British colonial rule in India.
 
• **Decline of the Movement:** The abolition of the Caliphate by Mustafa Kemal Atatürk in 1924 marked the end of the Khilafat Movement.
 
• **Legacy:** While the movement did not achieve its goal, it strengthened Hindu-Muslim unity temporarily and contributed to India's independence movement.

questions.question: Who is the Cabinet Secretary of India as of September 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__TV Somanathan__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• T. V. Somanathan (born 10 May 1965) is an Indian bureaucrat and IAS officer who is serving as the Cabinet Secretary of India since 30 August 2024. 
 
• Before this, he served as the Finance Secretary of India (Department of Expenditure).
 
• Prior to this appointment, he served as Additional Secretary and Joint Secretary in the Prime Minister's Office (PMO).
 
• He also worked as Director at the World Bank Group, Washington D.C., where he initially joined under its Young Professionals Program.
 
• He is a 1987 batch Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer of the Tamil Nadu cadre.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Role of the Cabinet Secretary:**

 
 
• Acts as the principal coordinator between the Union Government and various ministries/departments.
 
• Heads the Cabinet Secretariat and facilitates decision-making at the highest level of governance.
 
• Advises the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers on policy matters and administrative decisions.
 
 
 
• **Appointment Process:**
 
 
• The Cabinet Secretary is appointed by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC), chaired by the Prime Minister.
 
• The tenure is generally fixed at two years, but extensions can be granted based on performance and necessity.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The post of Cabinet Secretary was established in 1950, with N. R. Pillai being the first to hold the position.
 
• It is considered the apex post in the Indian civil service hierarchy.
 
 
 
• **Cabinet Secretariat:**
 
 
• It functions as the administrative arm of the Cabinet and handles major inter-ministerial coordination.
 
• It ensures smooth communication and implementation of decisions taken by the Union Council of Ministers.

questions.question: What change was observed in agricultural practices after the Green Revolution?

options.text: Focus on monoculture of wheat only
Decrease in the use of fertilisers
Shift from low-yield to high-yield crops
Shift from cash crops to subsistence farming

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shift from low-yield to high-yield crops**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Green Revolution in India, initiated in the 1960s, led to a significant shift from **traditional low-yield crops** to high-yield varieties (HYVs) of crops, particularly wheat and rice.
 
• The introduction of HYVs was complemented by the use of chemical fertilizers, pesticides, and advanced irrigation techniques to enhance agricultural productivity.
 
• It resulted in a dramatic increase in food grain production, especially in states like Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh, transforming India from a food-deficient country to a food-surplus one.
 
• The focus was primarily on staple crops like wheat and rice, which were scientifically bred to produce higher yields, ensuring food security and reducing dependency on imports.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **High-Yield Varieties (HYVs):** These are genetically modified crops designed to produce higher yields than traditional varieties, requiring intensive use of fertilizers and irrigation.
 
• **Irrigation Techniques:** The Green Revolution encouraged the adoption of modern irrigation methods like canal systems and tube wells to ensure adequate water supply for crops.
 
• **Fertilizers and Pesticides:** Chemical fertilizers and pesticides became integral to the success of the Green Revolution, aiding in pest control and providing essential nutrients to crops.
 
• **Impact on Economy:** The increased agricultural output contributed to a rise in rural incomes, reduced poverty in certain regions, and boosted India's economic growth during the late 20th century.
 
• **Criticism of Monoculture:** While the Green Revolution improved food security, it also led to environmental issues like soil degradation, water scarcity, and loss of biodiversity due to the focus on monoculture farming.

questions.question: Which outcome is typically expected from a government's expansionary fiscal policy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Stimulation of economic growth**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Expansionary fiscal policy involves increasing government spending or reducing taxes to boost **aggregate demand** in the economy.
 
• The primary goal is to stimulate **economic growth**, especially during periods of economic slowdown or recession.
 
• By increasing public expenditure, the government encourages **job creation** and higher consumer spending.
 
• Tax cuts leave individuals and businesses with more disposable income, further fueling **consumption and investment.**
 
• This policy often leads to a **temporary rise in the fiscal deficit**, which is offset by the long-term economic benefits of growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fiscal Policy:**

 
 
• Fiscal policy refers to the use of government spending and taxation to influence the economy.
 
• It is categorized into two types: **expansionary** and **contractionary** fiscal policy.
 
 
 
• **Aggregate Demand:**
 
 
• Aggregate demand is the total demand for goods and services within an economy at a given overall price level and time.
 
• It includes consumption, investment, government spending, and net exports.
 
 
 
• **Multiplier Effect:**
 
 
• Increased government spending can have a multiplier effect, where the initial spending leads to multiple rounds of increased economic activity.
 
• This amplifies the overall impact of fiscal measures on GDP growth.
 
 
 
• **Challenges:**
 
 
• Expansionary fiscal policy can lead to **inflationary pressures** if the economy is already operating near its capacity.
 
• It may increase the government's **debt levels** if not managed prudently.

questions.question: A very heavy concentration of Malwa settlements of Chalcolithic period was found in the:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Central Narmada Basin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Central Narmada Basin is one of the richest regions in terms of Chalcolithic settlements, particularly those belonging to the Malwa culture.
 
• Malwa settlements are characterized by advanced pottery styles, including painted pottery with intricate designs.
 
• Excavations in this region have revealed evidence of agricultural practices, including the cultivation of wheat and barley.
 
• The sites in the Central Narmada Basin include significant findings such as tools made of copper and stone, indicating a transitional phase between the Stone Age and Metal Age.
 
• Prominent Chalcolithic sites in this region include Navdatoli and Daimabad, which provide insights into the socio-economic aspects of the Malwa culture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chalcolithic Period:** The Chalcolithic period refers to the phase of human history where copper began to be used alongside stone tools.
 
• **Malwa Culture:** This culture is one of the prominent Chalcolithic cultures in India, known for its distinctive painted pottery and advanced agricultural practices.
 
• **Navdatoli:** A key Chalcolithic site located near the Narmada River, offering evidence of early settlement patterns, agricultural activity, and craft production.
 
• **Daimabad:** A significant site in Maharashtra linked to the Malwa culture, known for its discovery of bronze artifacts including the famous "Bronze Chariot."
 
• **Geographical Significance:** The Narmada Basin provided fertile land, water resources, and access to raw materials, making it suitable for early human settlements and the growth of Chalcolithic cultures.

questions.question: How many points are awarded for Lona in Kabaddi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Two**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In Kabaddi, a **Lona** is awarded when the entire opposing team is declared out.
 
• A Lona in Kabaddi fetches the team **2 additional points** apart from the points scored for individual outs.
 
• The concept of Lona encourages teams to strategize and attempt to eliminate all the opposing players.
 
• The awarded 2 points for a Lona can play a crucial role in deciding the final outcome of the match, especially in close contests.
 
• These rules are governed by the **International Kabaddi Federation** (IKF) and are standardized across professional tournaments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kabaddi**:

 
 
• Kabaddi is a contact team sport originating from India and is now popular worldwide, particularly in South Asia.
 
• The game is played between two teams of seven players each, and the objective is to score points by raiding the opponent’s half and tagging players.
 
• Players must chant "Kabaddi" continuously during a raid to demonstrate controlled breathing.
 
 
 
• **Point System in Kabaddi:**
 
 
• Each player tagged by the raider earns the raider's team 1 point.
 
• Bonus points are awarded when specific conditions are met, such as crossing a bonus line during a raid.
 
• The defensive team earns points by successfully tackling the raider (known as a super tackle if done with 3 or fewer defenders).
 
 
 
• **Lona Importance:**
 
 
• The Lona rule incentivizes aggressive gameplay and teamwork.
 
• Teams often attempt to eliminate all opposing players for a strategic advantage.
 
 
 
• **International Kabaddi Federation (IKF):**
 
 
• The governing body that standardizes Kabaddi rules worldwide.
 
• Founded in 2004, the IKF organizes major international tournaments, including the Kabaddi World Cup.

questions.question: What does the Greek letter ν (nu) represent in physics?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Frequency of a wave**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Greek letter **ν (nu)** is commonly used in physics to denote the **frequency of a wave**, particularly in the context of electromagnetic waves and sound waves.
 
• Frequency is defined as the **number of oscillations or cycles per unit of time**, usually measured in Hertz (Hz), where 1 Hz equals 1 cycle per second.
 
• The relationship between the speed of a wave (v), its frequency (ν), and wavelength (λ) is given by the equation: **v = ν × λ**.
 
• In quantum mechanics, ν is also used to represent the frequency of photons, which is related to their energy by the equation **E = hν**, where h is Planck's constant.
 
• The symbol ν should not be confused with similar Greek letters like μ (mu), which represents different physical quantities such as permeability or reduced mass.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Frequency (ν):** Frequency is a fundamental property of waves, describing how often the wave oscillates. It is inversely proportional to the period (T) of the wave, where **ν = 1/T**.
 
• **Hertz (Hz):** The SI unit of frequency, named after Heinrich Hertz, where 1 Hz equals 1 cycle per second.
 
• **Wave Equation:** The wave equation **v = ν**× **× λ** establishes a relationship between the speed of the wave (v), its frequency (ν), and its wavelength (λ).
 
• **Applications of Frequency:** Frequency plays a crucial role in various fields, including telecommunications (radio and TV signals), acoustics (sound waves), and quantum mechanics (photon energy).
 
• **Planck's Equation:** In quantum mechanics, the energy of a photon is directly proportional to its frequency, represented by the equation **E = hν**, where h = 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s (Planck's constant).

questions.question: Who advocated that India would be truly independent only when the poorest of its people became free of human suffering?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahatma Gandhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mahatma Gandhi, often referred to as the "Father of the Nation" in India, emphasized the importance of uplifting the poorest sections of society.
 
• He believed that true independence would only be achieved when the most marginalized people were free from suffering, poverty, and injustice.
 
• This philosophy aligns with his concept of "Sarvodaya," meaning the welfare of all, which he passionately advocated throughout his life.
 
• Gandhi's vision for India included a focus on self-reliance, rural development, and the empowerment of the underprivileged, especially through non-violent means.
 
• He often referred to the poorest individuals as "Daridranarayan," symbolizing God in the form of the poor, and prioritized their well-being in his ideology.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sarvodaya:** A Gandhian principle meaning "universal uplift" or "progress for all," focusing on the well-being of the weakest sections of society.
 
• ** Mahatma Gandhi's economic philosophy, advocating that wealth should be held in trust and used for the welfare of society, particularly for the poor.
 
• Economic Self-Reliance:** Gandhi promoted the use of khadi (handwoven cloth) and village industries to make Indian villages self-sufficient and reduce dependence on industrialized economies.
 
• **Harijan Movement:** Gandhi worked tirelessly to uplift the "Harijans" (now referred to as Dalits or Scheduled Castes), emphasizing their inclusion in society and opposing untouchability.
 
• **Gandhi's Legacy:** His principles of non-violence, equality, and focus on the marginalized continue to inspire socio-economic reforms in modern India and across the world.

questions.question: Gombe Habba, celebrated in the state of Karnataka during Navaratri, is a festival of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**dolls**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Gombe Habba**, also known as the Doll Festival, is celebrated during the Navaratri festival in Karnataka.
 
• It involves the arrangement and display of **decorative dolls and figurines** on steps or platforms in households.
 
• This tradition is especially popular among families to showcase **art, culture, and stories from Indian mythology**.
 
• Gombe Habba is a way to pass on traditional values and stories to the next generation while celebrating the cultural heritage of Karnataka.
 
• The displayed dolls are often passed down through generations, making the practice a mix of cultural preservation and religious devotion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Navaratri Festival:** Navaratri, meaning "nine nights," is a major Hindu festival dedicated to the worship of Goddess Durga and her nine forms.
 
• **Significance of Dolls:** In Gombe Habba, the dolls symbolize divine beings, cultural stories, and social themes, reflecting a blend of devotion and creativity.
 
• **Steps Arrangement:** The dolls are typically arranged on odd-numbered steps (e.g., 3, 5, 7, or 9) in a tiered fashion, symbolizing ascension and order.
 
• **Regional Variations:** Similar doll festivals are celebrated in other southern states, such as Bommai Kolu in Tamil Nadu and Bommala Koluvu in Andhra Pradesh.
 
• **Community Bonding:** The festival fosters community interaction as families visit each other’s homes to view doll displays and exchange sweets and gifts.

questions.question: Padma Shri awardee of 2024, Mahabir Singh Guddu is a folk dancer from which Indian state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Haryana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mahabir Singh Guddu is a renowned folk dancer and Padma Shri awardee from the state of **Haryana**.
 
• He has contributed significantly to the promotion and preservation of Haryana's traditional folk dance forms, especially **Ragini and Haryanvi folk art**.
 
• The Padma Shri award, India's fourth-highest civilian honor, was conferred upon him in recognition of his **lifelong dedication to cultural artistry**.
 
• Haryana's folk dances are known for their vibrant energy and deep connection to rural traditions, with artists like Mahabir Singh Guddu playing a pivotal role in keeping these traditions alive.
 
• His work has not only gained national recognition but also inspired younger generations to embrace and promote **local cultural heritage**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Padma Awards:**

 
 
• The Padma Awards are among the highest civilian honors in India, categorized as Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Shri.
 
• They are awarded annually on Republic Day for exceptional contributions in various fields such as art, literature, science, sports, social work, and public affairs.
 
 
 
• **Haryana Folk Culture:**
 
 
• Haryana boasts a rich cultural heritage with popular folk dances including **Jhumar, Ghoomar, and Ragini**.
 
• Music and dance are integral to social and festive occasions in Haryana.
 
 
 
• **Ragini Tradition:**
 
 
• Ragini is a traditional Haryanvi folk art form that blends music, poetry, and storytelling.
 
• It often highlights social themes and is performed during village fairs and gatherings.
 
 
 
• **Preservation of Folk Art:**
 
 
• Artists like Mahabir Singh Guddu contribute to the preservation of folk art by conducting workshops and performances in rural and urban regions.
 
• Efforts to document and promote these traditions are crucial for safeguarding India's intangible cultural heritage.

questions.question: As per NFHS 5, what percentage of the Indian population was deprived of drinking water during the year 2019-21?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.0732**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5) conducted during 2019-21, **7.32% of the Indian population lacked access to basic drinking water facilities**.
 
• The survey highlights disparities in access to safe drinking water, particularly in rural areas compared to urban regions.
 
• NFHS-5 is a comprehensive survey conducted to assess health, nutrition, and infrastructure-related parameters across India.
 
• Access to safe drinking water is a critical indicator of public health and directly impacts the quality of life and overall development of the population.
 
• The government of India has launched various programs, like the **Jal Jeevan Mission**, to address water accessibility issues and improve water supply in rural areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Family Health Survey (NFHS)**

 
 
• NFHS is a large-scale, multi-round survey conducted in a representative sample of households throughout India.
 
• The survey provides crucial data on health, family welfare, and other emerging issues in India.
 
• NFHS-5 was conducted between 2019 and 2021, covering all 707 districts of India.
 
 
 
• **Jal Jeevan Mission**
 
 
• Launched in 2019, Jal Jeevan Mission aims to provide functional household tap connections (FHTCs) to every rural household by 2024.
 
• The mission focuses on sustainable water supply systems through the creation of local infrastructure.
 
• It also promotes water conservation and rainwater harvesting.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Lack of Drinking Water**
 
 
• Access to unsafe water can lead to waterborne diseases like diarrhea, cholera, and typhoid.
 
• It can also affect hygiene practices, particularly in rural and underserved regions.
 
• Lack of clean drinking water disproportionately affects women and children, who are often responsible for water collection in rural areas.
 
 
 
• **Safe Drinking Water Definition**
 
 
• As per WHO guidelines, safe drinking water is water that is free of contaminants, harmful chemicals, and pathogens.
 
• Safe drinking water is essential for maintaining health and preventing waterborne diseases.

questions.question: Who was the first to introduce Brazilian bossa nova rhythm in Hindi film music?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**RD Burman**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **RD Burman** was the first to introduce the Brazilian bossa nova rhythm into Hindi film music.
 
• Bossa nova, which means "new trend" in Portuguese, is a Brazilian music style blending samba and jazz, and RD Burman incorporated it innovatively into Bollywood music.
 
• An iconic example of this rhythm in Hindi music is the song **"Maar Dalega Dard-e-Jigar" from the film "Pati Patni" (1966).**
 
• RD Burman’s creative genius was instrumental in infusing global music styles like bossa nova into Indian soundscapes, marking a transformative era in Hindi cinema music.
 
• This fusion of international rhythms with Indian melodies contributed significantly to RD Burman's legacy as a revolutionary music composer in Indian cinema.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bossa Nova:** A Brazilian music style that emerged in the late 1950s, characterized by a syncopated rhythm and smooth, melodic tones blending samba and jazz.
 
• **RD Burman’s Musical Legacy:** Known as the "Music Maverick," RD Burman introduced several global influences into Indian music, including reggae, funk, and disco, apart from bossa nova.
 
• **Global Influence in Bollywood Music:** During the 1960s-1980s, Indian film music began incorporating international music styles, largely due to composers like RD Burman.
 
• **Fusion in Film Music:** RD Burman’s approach to music was a pioneering mix of Indian classical, folk, and international styles, making his compositions timeless.
 
• **Brazilian Music Influence:** Beyond bossa nova, Brazilian samba and carnival rhythms occasionally influenced Bollywood music during the 20th century.

questions.question: As of October 2024, who is the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Girish Chandra Murmu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Girish Chandra Murmu** has been serving as the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India since **August 8, 2020**.
 
• He succeeded **Rajiv Mehrishi** as the 14th CAG of India.
 
• Girish Chandra Murmu is a 1985-batch IAS officer of the Gujarat cadre and has held several key positions in the Indian government, including the first Lieutenant Governor of Jammu and Kashmir.
 
• The CAG of India is appointed by the President of India under Article 148 of the Constitution.
 
• The CAG is responsible for auditing the accounts of the Union and state governments and ensuring accountability in public financial management.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Role of the CAG:** The CAG audits government accounts, ensures transparency, and submits reports to the President or Governors, which are then tabled in Parliament or state legislatures.
 
• **Article 148:** This article of the Indian Constitution establishes the position of the Comptroller and Auditor General and outlines its duties and powers.
 
• **Audit Scope:** The CAG audits expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India, state consolidated funds, and public sector undertakings (PSUs).
 
• **Independence of CAG:** The CAG enjoys complete independence, with provisions for security of tenure and immunity from arbitrary removal during its term.
 
• **International Recognition:** The CAG of India is a member of the International Organization of Supreme Audit Institutions (INTOSAI) and the Asian Organization of Supreme Audit Institutions (ASOSAI).

questions.question: Right to constitutional remedies as a Fundamental Right of the Constitution of India is stated in which of the following Articles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 32**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 32 of the Indian Constitution provides the right to constitutional remedies, empowering citizens to move the Supreme Court for enforcement of their Fundamental Rights.
 
• Dr. B.R. Ambedkar referred to Article 32 as the "heart and soul" of the Indian Constitution as it guarantees the protection of Fundamental Rights.
 
• Under Article 32, the Supreme Court can issue writs such as habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, and certiorari to enforce rights.
 
• This article ensures that no individual’s Fundamental Rights are violated without legal recourse.
 
• Article 32 is applicable only when there is a violation of Fundamental Rights, making it a cornerstone of judicial review in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Rights:** Enshrined in Part III of the Indian Constitution, these rights are guaranteed to all citizens and include rights such as equality, freedom, and protection from exploitation.
 
• **Types of Writs:** The writs issued under Article 32 include habeas corpus (protection against unlawful detention), mandamus (commanding public authority to perform its duty), prohibition (preventing lower courts from exceeding jurisdiction), certiorari (quashing orders of inferior courts), and quo warranto (challenging the legality of a public office).
 
• **Judicial Review:** Article 32 underlines the concept of judicial review, which allows the judiciary to ensure that laws and executive actions do not violate Fundamental Rights.
 
• **Supreme Court’s Role:** Article 32 exclusively empowers the Supreme Court to be the guardian of Fundamental Rights, though High Courts can enforce these rights under Article 226.
 
• **Article 226:** While Article 32 applies to the Supreme Court, Article 226 allows High Courts to issue writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights as well as other legal rights.

questions.question: How many types of plate tectonic boundaries are there?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Three**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• There are **three types of plate tectonic boundaries**: divergent, convergent, and transform boundaries.
 
• **Divergent boundaries** occur when plates move apart, leading to the formation of new crust (e.g., mid-ocean ridges).
 
• **Convergent boundaries** occur when plates collide, often resulting in mountain formation or subduction zones (e.g., Himalayas or Mariana Trench).
 
• **Transform boundaries** occur when plates slide past one another horizontally, causing earthquakes (e.g., San Andreas Fault).
 
• These boundaries are driven by the movement of tectonic plates due to **mantle convection, slab pull, and ridge push**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tectonic Plates:** Large sections of Earth's lithosphere divided into rigid plates that float on the semi-fluid asthenosphere below.
 
• **Mid-Ocean Ridges:** Underwater mountain ranges formed at divergent boundaries, where magma rises to create new crust.
 
• **Subduction Zones:** Areas where one plate is forced beneath another at convergent boundaries, often causing volcanic activity.
 
• **Earthquakes:** Commonly associated with transform boundaries, where stress builds up as plates move past each other.
 
• **Plate Movement Drivers:** Mantle convection (heat-driven fluid motion), slab pull (gravity pulling a subducting plate), and ridge push (force exerted by magma at divergent boundaries) are key mechanisms behind plate tectonics.

questions.concept: Ecology and Functions of an ecosystem
questions.question: In a forest ecosystem of Grass → Impala → Hyena, if all the Hyenas are taken away, what will happen ultimately?

options.text: Grass land will not be affected.
Impala will die of starvation due to higher population.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Impala will die of starvation due to higher population**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Hyenas are predators** in the forest ecosystem responsible for controlling the population of Impalas.
 
• With the removal of Hyenas, the **Impala population will grow unchecked**, leading to overpopulation.
 
• Overpopulation of Impalas increases competition for **limited resources like grass**, causing depletion of food supply.
 
• The lack of adequate food will result in starvation, leading to a decline in the Impala population over time.
 
• Such disturbances demonstrate the **interdependence of species** in an ecosystem and the importance of predators in maintaining ecological balance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Forest Ecosystems:** These are complex systems consisting of producers (grass), consumers (Impala), and predators (Hyena), which maintain ecological balance through food chains.
 
• **Role of Predators:** Predators control the population of herbivores, preventing overgrazing and ensuring the sustainability of vegetation.
 
• **Food Chain Dynamics:** In a food chain, removal of any species disrupts the flow of energy and resource availability, leading to ecological imbalance.
 
• **Carrying Capacity:** The maximum population size that an environment can sustain without depleting resources; exceeding this limit results in starvation and population collapse.
 
• **Trophic Levels:** Each level in a food chain represents energy transfer; producers (grass), primary consumers (Impala), and secondary consumers (Hyena) are interconnected.

questions.question: In tennis, the court should be _________ wide for a doubles match as per the International Tennis Federation.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**36ft**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the International Tennis Federation (ITF), the standard width of a tennis court for doubles matches is **36 feet (10.97 meters)**.
 
• The doubles court is wider than the singles court, which measures **27 feet (8.23 meters) in width**, to accommodate the additional players on each team.
 
• The total length of a doubles tennis court remains the same as a singles court: **78 feet (23.77 meters)**.
 
• The extra width in doubles courts is provided by the “doubles alleys,” which are the areas between the singles sidelines and the doubles sidelines.
 
• The court dimensions for doubles are consistent across all levels of play, from amateur to professional, as regulated by the ITF.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **International Tennis Federation (ITF):**

 
 
• The ITF is the governing body of world tennis and is responsible for defining and maintaining the rules of the game.
 
• It ensures consistent court dimensions and standards across international tournaments.
 
 
 
• **Doubles Alley:**
 
 
• The area on a tennis court between the singles and doubles sidelines, used only in doubles matches.
 
• The width of the doubles alley on each side is 4.5 feet (1.37 meters), making the total extra width 9 feet (2.74 meters).
 
 
 
• **Standard Court Surface Types:**
 
 
• The main types of tennis court surfaces are clay, grass, and hard courts, each affecting the speed and bounce of the ball.
 
• The dimensions of the court remain the same regardless of the surface type.
 
 
 
• **Key Court Markings:**
 
 
• **Baseline:** The back boundary line of the court, running parallel to the net.
 
• **Sidelines:** The outer boundaries of the court that vary for singles and doubles matches.
 
• **Service Boxes:** The rectangular areas on each side of the net where the serve must land.
 
 
 
• **Net Height:**
 
 
• The net height at the center is **3 feet (0.914 meters)**, and at the posts, it is **3.5 feet (1.07 meters).**
 
• The net divides the court into two equal halves for play.

questions.question: Which of the following classical dance forms from southern India derives its textual sanction from 'Balarama Bharatam' and 'Hastalakshana Deepika'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathakali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kathakali** is a classical dance-drama form that originated in Kerala, India, and is renowned for its elaborate costumes, face painting, and expressive gestures.
 
• The textual foundation of Kathakali is derived from two ancient treatises: **'Balarama Bharatam'**, which focuses on classical dance and drama, and **'Hastalakshana Deepika'**, which explains the gestures and hand movements.
 
• Kathakali combines elements of dance, music, and acting, rooted in themes from **Indian epics like the Mahabharata and Ramayana**.
 
• The art form employs intricate facial expressions and a vocabulary of hand gestures called **mudras**, which are codified in the 'Hastalakshana Deepika'.
 
• Kathakali is performed traditionally as a temple art and later evolved into a theatrical art form performed in open-air theatres.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Balarama Bharatam**: An ancient Sanskrit text attributed to Karthika Thirunal Balarama Varma, focusing on the theory and practice of natya (drama) and nritya (dance).
 
• **Hastalakshana Deepika**: A seminal treatise that codifies the hand gestures or mudras used in Kathakali and other traditional Indian dance forms.
 
• **Costume and Makeup**: Kathakali performers wear intricate and colorful costumes, including large headdresses, and apply elaborate facial makeup to depict various characters like gods, demons, and humans.
 
• **Musical Accompaniment**: The performance is accompanied by traditional percussion instruments like the **chenda** and **maddalam**, along with vocalists narrating the story.
 
• **Training and Rigorous Practice**: Kathakali artists undergo years of intense training, focusing on body flexibility, facial expressions, and synchronization of gestures with music and rhythm.

questions.question: No money bill can be introduced in the State Legislative Assembly without the prior permission of the ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Governor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A Money Bill can only be introduced in the State Legislative Assembly **with the prior permission of the Governor**.
 
• As per Article 207 of the Constitution of India, the Governor's recommendation is mandatory for introducing Money Bills in the State Legislature.
 
• The Money Bill deals with matters such as the imposition, abolition, remission, alteration, or regulation of taxes, borrowing of money by the state, and matters related to the Consolidated Fund of the State.
 
• The Governor acts as the formal authority for legislative proposals involving state finances, ensuring they align with constitutional provisions.
 
• Without the Governor's recommendation, a Money Bill cannot proceed in the legislative process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Money Bill:**

 
 
• It is defined under Article 110 of the Indian Constitution (at the Union level) and Article 199 (at the State level).
 
• A Money Bill exclusively deals with financial matters like taxation, appropriation of funds, and public expenditure.
 
• It can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha (Union) or State Legislative Assembly (State) and requires prior recommendation from the President (Union) or Governor (State).
 
 
 
• **Role of the Governor:**
 
 
• The Governor is the constitutional head of the state and acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers.
 
• In financial matters, the Governor ensures compliance with constitutional provisions by granting or withholding consent for legislative proposals.
 
 
 
• **State Legislature:**
 
 
• It comprises the Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) and, in some states, the Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad).
 
• The Legislative Assembly is the lower house where Money Bills are introduced and deliberated upon.
 
 
 
• **Legislative Process for Money Bills:**
 
 
• A Money Bill, after being introduced in the Legislative Assembly with the Governor's consent, goes through a detailed legislative process including debate, approval, and assent.
 
• The Legislative Council, if present, can only make recommendations and cannot amend or reject a Money Bill.
 
• After approval, it requires the Governor's assent to become law.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are INCORRECT?

i. The 'SGSY' scheme was implemented in 2009.

ii. The primary objective of the 'SGSY' scheme was to promote and attain self employment.

iii. The 'SGSY' scheme performed well in Andhra Pradesh.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Swarnjayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY)** was launched in **1999**, not 2009, making statement i incorrect.
 
• The primary objective of SGSY was to promote **self-employment** by organizing rural poor into Self-Help Groups (SHGs), making statement ii correct.
 
• SGSY showed significant success in states like Andhra Pradesh due to effective implementation, making statement iii correct.
 
• Since statement i is the only incorrect one, the correct option is **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Swarnjayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY)**:

 
 
• SGSY was introduced in **1999** as a holistic program for poverty alleviation.
 
• It aimed at promoting self-employment by organizing rural poor into **Self-Help Groups (SHGs)**.
 
• The scheme focused on **skill development, infrastructure creation, and bank linkage.**
 
• It was later restructured into the **National Rural Livelihood Mission (NRLM)** in 2011.
 
 
 
• **Self-Help Groups (SHGs)**:
 
 
• SHGs are small groups of individuals from similar socio-economic backgrounds who come together to form savings and credit groups.
 
• They play a critical role in empowering rural women and promoting financial inclusion.
 
 
 
• **National Rural Livelihood Mission (NRLM)**:
 
 
• NRLM replaced SGSY in 2011 to provide a more focused and comprehensive approach to rural poverty alleviation.
 
• It emphasizes community-driven approaches and the formation of SHGs.
 
 
 
• **Key Success Factors in Andhra Pradesh:**
 
 
• Effective implementation through strong community institutions.
 
• Active involvement of women in SHGs.
 
• Focus on livelihood diversification and skill development.
